    """
    Call stack of a linear search for element of the array

    This call stack will be our reference, and will we're simulating the conditions
    of the recursive function that searches for the key.
    """

    def search(low, high):
        # Base case of the search, only have to propagate two item-nums for the list
        """
        Use a global return so the two negative values aren't being overwritten for this recursive calls
        The global return for [first, last] is going to not be overwritten by calling the function recursively
        """
        global first, last #set first and last as global variables so they can be overwritten by recursive calls
        if low > high:
            # Out of bounds -> returns two negative values so Python knows there is not element
            return [-1, -1]
        
        # Mid element of nums we are recurslly going to evaluate each iterate
        mid = int((low + high) / 2)

        """
        Check if the key is at nums[mid] or if the value of the element stored in nums is <= the target.

        Algorithm strategy uses a divided and conquer approach below, so recursion used to divide and conquer the array of numbers to be searched through
        """
        if target == nums[mid]:
            return [mid, mid]
        
        # Recursively call if target is greater than nums in [mid]
        if target > nums[mid]:
            # Calls to search again in a full recursive call for the split array to the right of nums[mid]

            # Calls to search again in a full recursive call for the split array to the right of nums[mid]

        nums: A list of integers sorted in non-decreasing order.
        target: An integer.

    Returns:
        A list [first, last] holding the first and the last index at which target occurs in nums,
        or [-1, -1] if target does not occur.
    """
    first = -1
    last = -1

    # Find the first occurrence using binary search
    low = 0
    high = len(nums) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if nums[mid] == target:
            first = mid
            high = mid - 1  # Continue searching on the left for the first occurrence
        elif nums[mid] < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1

    # Find the last occurrence using binary search
    low = 0
    high = len(nums) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if nums[mid] == target:
            last = mid
            low = mid + 1  # Continue searching on the right for the last occurrence
        elif nums[mid] < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1

    return [first, last]
